newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ARGENTINE BONDS MIXED IN DULL TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ARGENTINE BONDS MIXED IN DULL TRADE.

text.p: Argentine bonds were mixed in dull late trade Monday, with the market sapped of volume ahead of U.S. retail sales figures due Wednesday, traders said.
"It wouldn't have mattered a jot if we hadn't come in to work today," one trader said. "There was very little volume."
He said the lack of trading insulated the market against variations in the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond, which hit its highest level for more than a month at 6.69 percent at one point in the session.
Argentina's Par Brady bond edged up 1/8 to 73-5/8. The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was down $0.65 at 119.
In the money market, one-week peso BAIBOR, or Buenos Aires interbank offered rate, was unchanged at 6.875 percent.
